title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π_0 is π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} over Q̄. M = Π_0^{ab} is generated by the loop classes λ_0, λ_1, λ_∞, with λ_0+λ_1+λ_∞ = 0, so M is free of rank 2 on λ_0, λ_1. The underlining suggests M is treated as a group scheme: Γ(−) means its points or sections, and the notation 'G_a ≃ L_0' in (121) suggests an additive, possibly pro-unipotent or Malcev-type, completion. This reading is uncertain.

ρ and σ are lifts of the generators of the S_3 symmetries of the three-punctured line. The computation fixes how they act on M:
- ρ_M: λ_0→λ_1, λ_1→λ_∞, so ρ is the 3-cycle 0→1→∞.
- σ_M: λ_0→λ_1, λ_1→λ_0, so σ is the involution z↦1−z, fixing ∞.

N_{ρ,σ} appears to be a group of pairs (α, β) of 'twisting' elements that modify ρ and σ. These pairs are subject to a compatibility condition, the 'relation des bouts' (relation of ends/tangential basepoints), whose abelianized form is (1−ρ_M)(α) = (1−σ_M)(β).

The question of §5 is: which inner automorphisms lie in N_{ρ,σ}? For l in Γ M_0, int(l) acts trivially on M_0. Tautologically int(l) corresponds to α = β = l (eq. 118). The ends relation then becomes ρ_M(l) = σ_M(l). Writing l = c_0λ_0 + c_1λ_1 (eq. 119):
- ρ_M(l) = c_0λ_1 + c_1λ_∞ = −c_1λ_0 + (c_0−c_1)λ_1;
- σ_M(l) = c_1λ_0 + c_0λ_1;
- equality forces 2c_1λ_0 + c_1λ_1 = 0, hence c_1 = 0.

So l ∈ L_0^M := Im(Z→M, c ↦ cλ_0), the inertia/cusp line at 0. This is exactly the line where ρ_M and σ_M agree (both send λ_0 to λ_1).

Result (121): an embedding G_a ≃ L_0^{M_0} → N_{ρ,σ}, together with the map L_0 → G^+ (written 𝔖^+ on the page). The next page checks that the image is normal and that the two resulting actions on G^+ coincide. One then forms the pushout-type quotient M_{ρ,σ} = N_{ρ,σ}/L_0, an extension of Γ_{ρ,σ} by G^{+a}, and a variant M^♮_{ρ,σ} with G^+ replaced by M. This is a standard 'extension modulo a central/inner part' construction for building the outer-type groups that act on the tower of fundamental groups of M_{0,3} (Teichmüller tower, base level).
errors: The equation-solving is correct: 2c_1λ_0 + c_1λ_1 = 0 forces c_1 = 0 in the free module on λ_0, λ_1. The '?' after ρ_M(l) = σ_M(l) is Grothendieck's own hesitation, which the computation then resolves.
Minor slip in the written line: '−c_*λ_0' should be −c_1λ_0. The page has it essentially right.
Gap: the reduction of the ends relation to its abelianized form (1−ρ_M)(α) = (1−σ_M)(β) is asserted, not derived on this page.

ideas.what: Determining which inner automorphisms are compatible with the S_3-symmetry lifts (ρ, σ) and the tangential-basepoint ('bouts') relation. The answer is the inertia line at 0.
ideas.modern_name: Inner/central part of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type normalizer; inertia subgroup at a cusp
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for the S_3 / ends relations in GT
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the circulated Longue Marche (1981); this continuation (pp. 650bis–787) is not in the usual circulated typescript as far as I know

ideas.what: Building M_{ρ,σ} as the quotient of N_{ρ,σ} by the inner part L_0, giving extensions of Γ_{ρ,σ} by G^{+a} or by M, possibly as group schemes.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of group extensions; outer-automorphism group of a (pro-unipotent?) fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group-extension technique; in the motivic setting Deligne (1989), Ihara

missed.claim: In the Longue Marche continuation, Grothendieck appears to set up the Teichmüller/GT-style groups attached to the S_3-symmetries of M_{0,3} as group schemes (G_a ≃ L_0^M). This would mean working with additive/pro-unipotent rather than only profinite objects, years before Deligne's 1989 motivic π_1 and Drinfeld's pro-unipotent GT. The reading of the notation is uncertain.
missed.quote: G_a ≃ L_0^{M_0} → N_{ρ,σ} ... d'après les topos généraux on trouve un schéma en groupes M_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If confirmed across neighbouring pages, it documents an early pro-algebraic treatment of the GT setup by Grothendieck, relevant to the history of GRT/GT. The content itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short, correct, routine computation within an unpublished section on Teichmüller/GT-type groups for P^1−{0,1,∞}. The only possibly notable feature is the group-scheme setting, which is historically interesting but uncertain and not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ𝕄_0' is better read as Γ M_0 (sections of the group scheme M_0), underlined M.
'on va-t-il [?] pour cela [?]' likely reads 'Mais il faut encore pour cela la relation des bouts', followed by a parenthetical relation 'μ = 1 dans ν'' = 0' (uncertain).
'Donc c'est nous retrouvons' reads roughly 'Donc nous retrouvons qu'on se restreint à l ∈ Γ L_0^{M_0}, correspondant aux conditions des...'.
In (120), beneath Z the symbols look like 'u' and 'G_a' (the identification Z ≃ G_a); the map is c_0 ↦ c_0λ_0.
(121) target in the down arrow is underlined 𝔖^+ / G^+ (the next page writes G^+).
